html:
Irazú is the highest volcano in Costa Rica, near the old capital of Cartago. From March 1963 to early 1965 it erupted again and again, covering San José and the Central Valley with ash.

The first big blast came days before a visit by President John F. Kennedy in March 1963. For two years ash fell on roofs, streets and fields. It damaged the coffee and vegetable harvests, and people swept ash from their houses every morning. Late in 1963 ash washed down the Reventado River in a mudflow that destroyed homes on the edge of Cartago.

The eruptions led to new flood walls and to closer watching of the country's many volcanoes. Irazú, like others on the isthmus, also made the soils that fed the Cartago valley and the farms of Costa Rica.
sum: Irazú is the highest volcano in Costa Rica, near the old capital of Cartago. From March 1963 to early 1965 it erupted again and again, covering San José and the Central Valley with ash.
